rationale.conceptual: The method combines tight-binding band structures, many-body Coulomb interactions with static Lindhard screening, solution of the exciton eigenvalue problem, and projection of electron-phonon coupling onto an excitonic basis. Each component is mathematically detailed and requires understanding of density-matrix formalism and correlation expansion. Translating the published equations into a consistent numerical workflow is research-grade and non-trivial, but builds on established semiconductor Bloch equations framework.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has about 5 sequential stages (geometry/k-grid, tight-binding bands, screened Coulomb/exciton solver, exciton-phonon coupling, absorption spectra extraction) with dependencies. No external tooling or data fetching is required; all parameters are given in the paper. This fits a multi-stage pipeline of moderate length with standard I/O.

Execution involves ~5 sequential computational steps with no exotic tooling or data fetching.
